text: Jane can implement a time management strategy for her writing hobby by leveraging the quiet periods in her day and breaking her writing process into manageable micro-tasks. Since she can only write when the house is quiet, she should identify specific windows of time, such as during her children’s naps, early mornings before they wake up, or late evenings after they are asleep. She can start by setting a realistic goal, such as writing for just 15–20 minutes during these quiet intervals, rather than aiming for long sessions. To maximize efficiency, she can use the busier times of her day for pre-writing activities that do not require silence, such as brainstorming plot ideas, outlining chapters, or researching topics on her phone or a notepad. Additionally, she can prepare her writing space in advance so that when quiet time arrives, she can start immediately without setup delays. By consistently dedicating small, focused bursts of time during these quiet moments and utilizing fragmented time for preparatory work, Jane can steadily progress with her short stories without overwhelming her busy schedule.
